title: Chronicle rollout orchestrator: deferred gated promotes with autorepair rollback advisor
author: Nina Alvarez
description:
Motivation: Customers need safer, resumable promotions from shadow to canary that preserve session affinity and allow automated, explainable rollback suggestions when regression signals appear. This change introduces the 'Chronicle' rollout orchestrator: a deferred, gate-driven promote controller that combines session-coherent shadow draining, synthetic dry-run replays, and an autorepair rollback advisor that surfaces prioritized rollback actions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a new orchestration runtime (chronicle-controller) and associated API surface for declarative deferred promotes. Chronicle implements: deferred promote windows (start/hold/commit phases), gate predicates (latency/error/quality thresholds), session-coherent handoff (keeps user sessions sticky until safe promote point), synthetic dry-run (replay a sample of live traffic through candidate model variants without affecting live responses), rollout telemetry anchors (time-series anchors for counterfactual comparison), and the Autorepair rollback advisor which synthesizes a ranked list of rollback playbooks with a confidence score. The description includes a short checklist: [x] controller runtime and CRD definitions, [x] controller unit + integration tests, [x] synthetic-replay harness (v0), [x] observability wiring (metrics/traces/logs), [x] migration docs and playbook.

Implementation notes: The controller is written in Go, uses the existing servegraph APIs for traffic routing, and introduces a lightweight playback worker that taps sampled requests (configurable sample rate) and replays them to candidate pools with deterministic session keys. We extended the promote API with three new fields: deferredWindow (start/hold/commit timestamps), gateProfiles (list of metric predicates with tolerances), and repairPolicy (auto|suggest|manual). The Autorepair advisor subscribes to the controller's telemetry stream, runs diff diagnostics (latency P50/P95, token-level quality regressions from eval hooks, error-rate deltas), and emits a ranked set of rollback actions (e.g., instant-swap revert, staged-drain to shadow, model-variant fallback) together with a recommended explanation string.

Backward compatibility and migration: Chronicle is opt-in; existing rollout CRs are unchanged. We added a migration guide under docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md and a console flag to enable the UI promote flow.

Risks & mitigations: Risk: synthetic replay could increase cost. Mitigation: sample rate defaults to 0.1% and is configurable per rollout. Risk: mis-ranked rollback suggestions. Mitigation: initial advisor run is suggest-only; we surface confidence and require two reviewers to enable auto mode.

Related work: builds on prior rollout work (see ENG-1427 for canary gating ideas, ENG-2131 for session affinity improvements). Links: linear/ENG-2147, design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2147/chronicle-rollout-design, runbook draft: docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md.

Notes for reviewers: focus on controller reconciliation correctness, telemetry anchors calculation, and the advisor’s ranking heuristic. I included unit and integration test summaries further down.

review_comments: Aaron Chen (2024-11-06): Question - how does the playback worker guarantee deterministic ordering for session-affine replays? Can we avoid adding latency to the serving path when sampling?

Nina Alvarez (2024-11-06): Reply - playback uses an async tap; we only capture headers + body snapshot. Determinism is achieved via a stable session hash (user-id || cookie) and a per-rollout replay queue. No sync blocking on request path. Added notes in playback/worker.go comments.
Priya Rao (2024-11-08): Request changes - the advisor ranking currently favors latency regressions over token-level quality; please make weighting configurable and add unit tests for rank stability.
Nina Alvarez (2024-11-09): Update - added advisor weight config (advisor.weighting.latency, .quality, .error) with defaults and unit tests for stability under small signal noise.

Lucas Green (2024-11-10): Suggestion - add an opt-in dry-run flag that emits the rollback suggestion to the audit log only (no auto actions). This will help SRE validate suggestions during initial rollout.
Nina Alvarez (2024-11-10): Done - added repairPolicy 'suggest' which writes advisor decisions to audit logs and surfaces them in the console. Updated runbook with verification steps.
Priya Rao (2024-11-11): Approved - tests look good, minor nits addressed.
Aaron Chen (2024-11-12): Approved - verified e2e smoke on staging cluster. CI green.
release_notes: Introduces 'Chronicle' rollout orchestrator (opt-in). Features: deferred gated promotes, session-coherent handoff, synthetic dry-run replays, and an Autorepair rollback advisor (suggest-only by default). See docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md for migration steps and console enablement.
notes_for_ops: Default playback sample rate is conservative (0.1%). Advisor auto-mode disabled by default; to enable, set helm value 'chronicle.advisor.mode=auto' and require two reviewer approvals in policy. Monitor metrics 'chronicle_gate_failures' and 'chronicle_advisor_confidence'.
test_summary: Unit tests added for gate predicate engine and advisor ranking. Integration test validates full deferred window lifecycle including commit and staged rollback. Manual staging smoke run performed on staging cluster with 1000 sampled replays.
